issues.description: Method return type mismatch for SealSaloon.checkOrderReady(): The problem statement (UML in problem_statement.md) declares checkOrderReady() with return type void (see UML method entry), but the reference solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java) defines public boolean checkOrderReady() (returns boolean). This inconsistency can confuse students about the required method signature and whether a return value should be implemented or used by callers.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent between the specification and the implementation. Two options: (A) Update the problem statement UML and any textual mentions to declare checkOrderReady() as returning boolean and document the meaning of the boolean return value (e.g., true if at least one order was served). OR (B) Change the solution implementation to public void checkOrderReady() (remove the boolean return and adjust internal logic/callers accordingly). Prefer option B if the boolean return value is not required by tests, so the implementation matches the declared API in the problem statement.
